manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Pick up the green orange and place it in the bowl.

Task description: Use the right gripper to pick up the green orange at the lower left of the fruit pile in the head-camera view and place it in the light blue-green bowl on the right.

Success criteria: The green orange is stable inside the bowl, and the gripper is open and no longer holding it.

## Execution tips

- Consider approaching the green orange from an open area above it. Adjust the gripper opening to the fruit’s width and surrounding clearance, avoiding the yellow fruit on its right and the orange fruit behind it.
- Place the pads against the wider sides around the orange's middle. Before closing, use both views to confirm the fruit is between the fingers, avoiding a grasp only on its curved top that could slip.
- During transport, leave clearance between the orange's base and neighboring fruit and the bowl rim. If adjusting its pose, do so in open space to reduce contact with the fingers.
- During placement, bring the orange inside the bowl opening and near the bottom until supported before opening the gripper, avoiding a direct drop from above the rim that could cause bouncing. Withdraw the fingers clear of the wall to avoid moving the bowl or fruit.

narration: I will use the piper-control skill for this authorized real-robot episode, strictly following the given parameters and acting on the returned manual and live observations.

I have confirmed the target is the green orange at the lower left of the fruit pile and the target container is the light blue-green bowl on the right. I am adjusting the approach pose above the fruit, then will align gradually and check the grasp.

A pose adjustment reached the joint range, and the controller returned a recoverable rejection; the arm is stationary. From the current measured position, I will continue approaching with a smaller tilt angle to avoid the limit.

The joint limit has been avoided and the gripper is directly above the green orange. Next I will descend in steps no larger than 1 cm and adjust finger direction to leave clearance from the adjacent yellow fruit.

The finger orientation has been adjusted, and the green orange is inside the gripper opening. I am lowering gradually to the side of the fruit; after closing, I will make a small lift to confirm it moves with the gripper before carrying it.
The gripper has closed to about 45.5 mm, and the fingers contact both sides of the green orange. I will first lift it by 1 cm to check whether the grasp is secure.

During the test lift, the orange remained on the table, indicating the grasp was not secure. I reopened the gripper and will lower the grasp point so the pads contact a wider area on the sides before trying again.

During this test lift, the green orange moved off the table with the gripper and remains held. I will continue lifting high enough to clear the neighboring fruit and bowl rim, then move above the bowl opening.
The orange has been lifted to transport height and remains held in consecutive observations. I am moving above the bowl, then will align with the interior in small steps.
The gripper is near the bowl opening, and the orange remains securely grasped. Next I will align over the bowl center and lower in small steps, opening only after the orange is supported inside.
The orange is within the bowl opening, and the bowl has not moved. I am continuing to descend slowly, checking the gap between the orange and bowl bottom and between the fingers and bowl wall.
The orange has been lowered near the bottom of the bowl. I will open the gripper and withdraw upward slowly, watching whether the orange remains stable inside.

After retreating and waiting, the green orange remains stable in the bowl and the gripper stays open, with a measured opening of 66.4 mm. I will end the episode and read the recording directory; final success still requires on-site operator confirmation.
